title: Tobias Gregson Shows What He Can Do
question: Today, can a man be certain and wrong in the same room?

breakfast_morning.described: The first-floor sitting-room of 221B Baker Street, 1881: two broad sash windows in the FAR wall over Baker Street, a black iron grate under a white marble mantelpiece in the LEFT wall, the panelled door to the landing in the RIGHT wall, a red patterned Turkey carpet, buff striped wallpaper, a horsehair sofa along the near RIGHT wall, two worn armchairs at the hearth, a deal side table carrying a rack of test tubes and a spirit lamp, bookshelves flanking the chimney breast. A round breakfast table stands under the two windows with a white cloth, a coffee pot, two cups and a spread of folded newspapers across it, and the white morning light of an April day comes flat through the two sash windows and a small coal fire burns red in the black grate

shots.frame: Insert straight down on the white breakfast cloth: four folded newspapers spread across it with BRIXTON MYSTERY standing black across the top of the nearest column, a white coffee cup and its saucer at the edge of the cloth.
shots.motion: The camera pulls back off the newspapers across the whole shot, travelling a forearm; a bare hand comes into the bottom of frame and draws the nearest paper a thumb's width toward the camera; the fingers spread flat on the column.
shots.camera: straight down over the round table, level with a standing man's chin and a forearm above the cloth, a 50mm lens. The white morning light falls from the windows at the TOP
shots.at_rest: Four folded newspapers lie spread across a white cloth filling the whole frame, the black word BRIXTON standing at the height of a thumb across the nearest column, a white coffee cup and saucer stand at the RIGHT edge, and a bare hand rests at the BOTTOM edge of frame
shots.why: The chapter opens on the press, not on the men: the world has taken the case up and that is the new fact. An insert of the headline says it without a word.

shots.frame: Medium of the round breakfast table under the two sash windows: Holmes bare-headed in the bottle-green velvet jacket over a white shirt collar in the far chair with a paper open in both hands, Watson bare-headed, his thin waxed moustache dark on his sunburnt face, in the near chair in a grey tweed waistcoat with a paper folded on the cloth before him.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in on the two men across the whole shot, travelling two long strides; Holmes lowers his paper to the cloth and his chin comes up; Watson turns his head to him across the table.
shots.camera: at the hearth rug, level with a seated man's chest and four long strides from the table, a 35mm lens turned to the windows. The white morning light comes flat through the two sash windows behind them
shots.at_rest: A round table under a white cloth stands across the CENTRE of frame at the height of a man's hip, a man in a bottle-green velvet jacket sits in the far chair with an open newspaper held up before him at the height of his chest, a man in a grey tweed waistcoat sits in the near chair three-quarters to the camera, the two sash windows stand across the TOP with white morning light coming through them, and the red Turkey carpet holds the BOTTOM of frame
shots.why: Establishes the room and the pair at their ordinary hour, and shows Holmes entertained by what horrifies the public. That gap is the episode's engine.

shots.motion: The camera tracks a hand's breadth to the right across the whole shot; his chin comes up further; his free hand comes out toward the doorway at the height of his own shoulder.
shots.camera: at the hearth rug, level with a standing man's eyes and two long strides from him, a 50mm lens. The white morning light falls across his pale face from the LEFT
shots.at_rest: A tall long-limbed man's head and chest fill the LEFT of CENTRE at half the frame height with his chin up and his face turned to the RIGHT, a lit cigar stands between two fingers at the height of his chest, the open panelled door shows at the RIGHT edge, and the buff striped wallpaper is behind him
shots.turn: a rival arriving -> a rival to crow over

shots.frame: Close on Lestrade in the doorway, a little lean man with a dark sallow rat-like face and black eyes, his collar askew at his throat, the dim stairhead out of focus behind his head.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in on his face across the whole shot, travelling a forearm; his head comes up square to the room; his mouth opens on the line.
shots.camera: at the hearth rug, level with a standing man's eyes and two long strides from the doorway, an 85mm lens. The white morning light falls on one side of his face from the LEFT
shots.at_rest: A little lean man's head fills the CENTRE of frame at half the frame height with a sallow face under wavy chestnut hair and black eyes, his collar stands askew at his throat at the BOTTOM of frame, the panelled door jamb holds the LEFT edge, and the dim stairhead stands out of focus behind his head
shots.turn: a case closed -> a second murder
shots.why: The world answers, and it is not the lead who says it. Everything Gregson has spent two minutes building is gone in one sentence he does not get to argue with.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: The papers next morning were full of the Brixton Mystery, and every one of them was certain.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Holmes and I read the notices over together at breakfast, and they afforded him considerable amusement.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Whatever happened, he said, Lestrade and Gregson would both be sure to score by it.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: That depends on how it turns out, I said, and he told me it hardly mattered.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Then came a pattering of many feet in the hall, and our landlady's loud disgust with it.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Six of the dirtiest, most ragged street boys I ever clapped eyes on rushed into the room.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: In future, he told them, Wiggins alone should come up, and the others keep to the street.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: He handed each of them a shilling, and they scampered off downstairs like so many rats.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: There is more work in one of those little beggars, he said, than in a dozen police.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Here is Gregson, he said, coming down the road with beatitude on every feature of his face.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: There was a violent peal at the bell, and the fair-haired detective came up three at a time.

lines.speaker: tobias_gregson
lines.text: Congratulate me! I have made the whole thing as clear as day.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: A shade of anxiety crossed Holmes's expressive face, and I heard him ask for the name.

lines.speaker: tobias_gregson
lines.text: Arthur Charpentier, sub-lieutenant in Her Majesty's navy, under lock and key.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Holmes gave a sigh of relief, and offered the man a cigar and some whiskey and water.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: He had begun, he told us, with the dead man's hat and the maker's name inside it.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Underwood of Camberwell Road had sent that hat to a boarding house in Torquay Terrace.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: No good comes of falsehood, the daughter said, and owned that they had seen Drebber again.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: He had come back that night the worse for drink, and caught the girl by the wrist.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Her brother came through the door with a stout oak cudgel in his hand.

lines.speaker: tobias_gregson
lines.text: I flatter myself that I have managed it rather neatly.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: He had arrested the young man with the cudgel still upon him, and thought the case complete.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Well done, said Holmes in an encouraging voice; we shall make something of you yet.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Then Lestrade came up our stairs, and all the jauntiness had gone out of his dress.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Gregson crowed at him, and asked whether he had managed to find the secretary Stangerson.

lines.speaker: g_lestrade
lines.text: Joseph Stangerson was murdered at Halliday's Private Hotel about six o'clock this morning.
